title: You Can't Outrun a Grizzly Bear: It Can Run as Fast as a Racehorse 🐻 (Would Meatball Survive? #3)
description:
Can you outrun a grizzly bear? The U.S. National Park Service says bears can run as fast as a racehorse, uphill and down, and that they will chase fleeing animals like dogs do, so do not run. If a grizzly attacks, the Park Service says to play dead: flat on your stomach, hands clasped behind your neck, pack on. Alaska's bear-safety guide narrows that to a defensive bear that has knocked you down, and calls it rarely necessary. If the attack keeps going, or the bear stalked you then attacked or attacked in your tent, fight back. Per the Park Service, a black bear attack is different: do not play dead. The Park Service also says no single strategy works in every situation.

#grizzlybear #bears #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: U.S. National Park Service (Staying Safe Around Bears); Glacier National Park (Bear Safety); Alaska Department of Fish and Game (Framework for Bear Safety Messages). General information, not safety training.
